original_description: Maps rippling effects of decisions across domains by tracing first, second, and third-order consequences and identifying feedback loops. Use this skill whenever the user needs impact analysis, wants to understand consequences of a decision, says "what are the effects of", "how will this ripple", "impact analysis", "second-order effects", "cascade effects", "what could go wrong", or needs to evaluate a decision across multiple stakeholder domains. Also trigger for architecture decisions, product launches, policy changes, organizational restructuring, technology migrations, or process changes where effects cross boundaries.

final_description: Invoke this skill — do not answer freestyle — whenever someone presents a decision or change and asks about its broader consequences across multiple areas. This skill's structured cascade mapping methodology produces superior analysis to ad-hoc reasoning. Trigger for: budget cuts, tech migrations, reorgs, policy changes, pricing shifts, open-sourcing, competitive responses, RTO mandates, SDK deprecations, vendor switches, or ANY scenario where someone asks "what happens if we...", "what breaks downstream", "map the effects across", "ripple effects", or "what does this mean for [multiple teams/areas]". Not for writing code, PR reviews, documentation, or infrastructure setup.

history.description: Use this skill any time someone presents a specific decision or change and asks you to trace its consequences, downstream effects, or cross-domain impact. The user has made (or is considering) a concrete action — budget cuts, technology migrations, policy changes, org restructuring, pricing shifts, product pivots — and wants to systematically understand what happens next across multiple teams, functions, or stakeholder groups. Invoke this skill when the request goes beyond "help me decide" into "help me see all the ways this plays out." Key signals: the user names a decision AND asks about effects on multiple areas, mentions ripple effects, downstream consequences, what breaks, or cross-team impact. Do NOT use for implementation tasks like writing code, reviewing PRs, creating docs, or setting up infrastructure — even if the word "cascade" appears.
